metadata.title: Towards the development of contextual questionnaires for the PISA for Development study (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD working paper is a methodological development and questionnaire-design document for enhancing PISA for Development (PfD) contextual questionnaires, not an empirical student-level analysis with reported model estimates. It discusses the PISA questionnaire framework, evolution of contextual measures across PISA cycles, and options for extending constructs (e.g., ESCS and school resources) to better fit low- and middle-income contexts. Because the paper does not report an analytic dataset with a defined analytic sample, it does not specify whether complex survey weights or replicate weights were applied. For any future empirical implementation of the proposed PfD questionnaires using PISA microdata, analysts should apply the complex survey design weights provided in the PISA database and follow PISA technical standards for variance estimation and scaling.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This paper does not conduct an empirical predictive analysis of cognitive achievement outcomes using PV-based dependent variables. Instead, it focuses on technical and conceptual issues in enhancing contextual questionnaire instruments (constructs, indices, and item themes) for PfD, including recommendations for measurement and pilot testing. As a result, plausible-value generation/combining and a missing-data handling strategy for PV-based outcomes are not part of the study’s reported methods.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level analytic sample is reported. The paper describes technical issues and measurement options based on a review of PISA contextual questionnaires (2000–2012) and a review of measures used in other international studies, plus stakeholder discussions; it does not specify inclusion/exclusion criteria for an empirical dataset.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education Working Paper provides a measurement and questionnaire-development roadmap for enhancing the PISA contextual questionnaires used in the PISA for Development (PfD) study. Rather than estimating effects on achievement, it synthesizes the PISA questionnaire framework (student, classroom, and school contexts), reviews how contextual measures evolved across PISA cycles (2000–2012), and compares constructs used in other international assessments relevant to low- and middle-income countries. The paper identifies seven enhancement themes—early learning opportunities, language at home and at school, family and community support, quality of instruction, learning time, socioeconomic status, and school resources—and discusses options for extending existing PISA scales (especially ESCS) while maintaining international comparability. It also outlines psychometric and pilot-testing requirements (including IRT-based analyses) and emphasizes integration constraints such as questionnaire length and the PfD assessment design (e.g., rotation).
data.null_fields_interpretation: The paper is a methodological development and instrument-design study rather than an empirical ML/predictive analysis. Consequently, it does not report a student-level analytic sample, PV handling, missing-data handling, or any ML model performance metrics. The extraction therefore leaves sample- and model-related fields empty while capturing the substantive methodological contributions in the outcome summary.
